headline: Ready for review as an optional, default-Off Windows CPU-efficiency setting; it does not fix PGR2 Vulkan lag.
scope: Same-build Off versus On measurements were collected on implementation 0edb216c23ab071042bb26005267d0c3816337cd. The wait implementation, UI/config wiring and focused tests are byte-identical in production source a0bb1187b4f49e7a790c770b0ced487d32eca99a, tree 4fef93d9750edee89485cea20698adf51773273a; that source only removes the dormant validation marker receiver. Production executable SHA-256 is 9df0a0f15d596c9e04ba2581ad4567271ac8679e4640b9d4328149beae320e60. Current PR head a2a444a85f29dab215bbd646ce1a32a690a9fd1b adds documentation. Cadence is an NV2A guest display-write proxy, not rendered FPS; lag rows are means of two run-level measurements per mode.

rows.note: 25.33% lower host CPU; higher is not better for this metric
Guest display-write proxy; Vulkan remains below 27/s

missing: No demonstrated PGR2 Vulkan lag fix; the measured Vulkan lag snapshot remains effectively neutral and below 27 display writes/s.
No universal power saving is established; the Vulkan board-power pair moved from 20.854 W Off to 21.425 W On.
The graph is representative; the existing PR body retains PGR2 CPU, device GPU, board power and all per-test rows.
